text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on February 9 in history.
1540 - The first recorded horse race meeting in England was held at Roodeye Fields, Chester.
1674 - Charles II of England signed the Treaty of Westminster, ending the war with the Dutch.
1773 - William Henry Harrison, ninth U.S. president, born. He was the first president to die in office, after only one month.
1801 - France and Austria signed the Peace of Luneville, effectively ending the Holy Roman Empire.
1849 - Giuseppe Mazzini proclaimed Rome a republic.
1863 - Anthony Hope, English novelist who wrote "Prisoner of Zenda", born.
1861 - Jefferson Davis was chosen as president, and Alexander Stephens as vice-president, of the Confederate States of America.
1881 - Fyodor Dostoyevski, Russian novelist, died. His novels included "Crime and Punishment", "The Idiot" and "The Brothers Karamazov", considered his finest.
1891 - Ronald Colman, English actor and Oscar winner for his role in "A Double Life", born in Richmond, Surrey.
1904 - At the outbreak of the Russo-Japanese War, the Russian ships Variag and Korietz were sunk off Korea.
1909 - France and Germany reached agreement over Morocco, with Germany recognising French special interests there in return for economic concessions.
1909 - Dean Rusk, U.S. secretary of state under both Presidents Kennedy and Johnson, born.
1923 - Dobrolet, the Soviet state airline, was formed. It was renamed Aeroflot in 1932.
1923 - Brendan Behan, Irish poet, novelist, playwright, and member of the IRA, born.
1926 - Garret FitzGerald, Irish politician, born. Leader of Fine Gael and prime minister 1981-82 and 1983-87, he helped to formulate and signed the Anglo-Irish Agreement.
1929 - The Litvinov protocol, a pact for the renunciation of war, was signed in Moscow between Russia, Poland, Romania, Estonia and Latvia.
1934 - The Balkan Pact to prevent encroachment by the great powers was signed by Romania, Greece, Yugoslavia and Turkey.
1941 - In a speech directed at the United States, Britain's wartime prime minister Winston Churchill said: "Put your confidence in us...give us the tools and we will finish the job".
1943 - U.S. troops reached Guadalcanal, Solomon Islands, and discovered the Japanese had evacuated.
1950 - U.S. senator Joseph McCarthy said he had evidence that there were individuals in the State Department who were card-carrying members of the Communist Party.
1969 - The first test flight of the Boeing 747 Jumbo Jet took place.
1971 - An earthquake measuring 6.6 struck the San Fernando Valley in California, killing 58 people. Property damage reached $900 million.
1972 - The British government declares a state of emergency over a miners' strike.
1977 - Sergei Vladimirovich Ilyushin, Russian aircraft designer, died.
1978 - Canada announced it was expelling 13 Soviet diplomats who it said had tried to recruit a Royal Canadian Mounted Police officer.
1981 - Bill Haley, legendary U.S. rock and roll singer, died.
1981 - General Wojciech Jaruzelski took over from Josef Pinkowski as Polish prime minister during the Solidarity crisis.
1983 - The racehorse Shergar, the 1981 English Derby winner, was stolen from his stable in Ireland.
1984 - Soviet leader Yuri Andropov died. A former KGB chief, he succeeded Leonid Brezhnev in late 1982 and was in power for less than 15 months.
1996 - A huge IRA bomb exploded in London's Docklands business district, killing two and injuring 100. The blast signalled the end of a 17-month IRA ceasefire.
